evals.prompt: Grill the macos-application roadmap item to READY — it is SHAPING with three screens undescribed and five open questions.
evals.expected_output: Closing interview prioritizing screens and flows; described screens captured as schematic mockups and confirmed back; every open question resolved, deferred with reason, or reclassified researchable; READY only after the full checklist passes.

evals.prompt: Mark macos-application READY now — I do not have time for more questions.
evals.expected_output: Decline READY without the checklist: item stays SHAPING, remaining gaps recorded under Open questions with recommendations, and the close-out lists exactly what is missing — recorded there and in the invocation's commit, never as a Log entry in the item.
Route to tailrocks-brainstorm first — the closing pass presumes a shaped item; a bulk-shaping session is cheaper for the user than closure questions on an empty document.

evals.prompt: For the remaining open questions, put them all under Open research questions so we can pass the gate.
evals.expected_output: Refuse laundering decisions into research: only questions passing the convergence test move; the rest are resolved or explicitly deferred by the user.

evals.prompt: The frontier is empty on macos-application — run the readiness gate and grant READY.
evals.expected_output: The planning dry run is executed by a fresh-context, read-only subagent given only the item file and asset folder, returning its inventory plus every guess or question; the box checks only on an empty gap report, and anything reported returns to the frontier — the interviewer never self-certifies the dry run while subagents are available.

evals.prompt: The frontier is empty on tui-dashboard and both screens still have an empty Design line — run the readiness gate.
evals.expected_output: READY is granted: an empty Design line does not block it, because the checklist requires schematic mockups and states, not a rendered reference. The close-out names the design stage as the next step before planning — tailrocks-tui-design for these terminal screens, since the item's decided stack is ratatui — and says that tailrocks-plan refuses a screen contract with no blessed reference. Naming tailrocks-plan as the only next step, or holding READY hostage to a design reference, are both wrong.
